deployTriggerFinding.claim: The dispatch states 'hauska-map does not [auto-deploy], but verify before assuming.' Verified: hauska-map's own git history includes a commit message citing an error 'found via Vercel build' (70ea0fe), and _catalog/seat_register.json repeatedly and explicitly notes 'No deploy' as a constraint on individual hauska-map lane worktrees (e.g. hauska-map-ctx-b4, hauska-map-p91-mark) -- language that would be unnecessary if a hauska-map merge could not trigger a deploy. property-explorer-ci.yml itself has no deploy step, consistent with Vercel's GitHub App doing deploys out-of-band on push, not through GH Actions.
deployTriggerFinding.conclusion: Contrary to the dispatch's premise, hauska-map/property-explorer most likely DOES deploy automatically via Vercel's GitHub integration on a merge to main -- this was not independently confirmed by reading Vercel project settings (no API access attempted; out of scope to chase further for a bug-fix lane), but the evidence available says 'verify before assuming' was warranted, and the honest position is 'probably deploys', not 'does not deploy'.
deployTriggerFinding.decision: Fix is pushed and a PR is open (#405) but NOT merged. Merging is being treated as equivalent to deploying for this repo, and 'Deploy without the operator's go' is on this dispatch's Do-Not list. This is the reason the dispatch's own required 'live re-read of the 97651/97652 pair through both the brief and the export panel' (post-fix) cannot be produced in this close -- it needs the fix to actually be serving, which needs a merge/deploy, which needs the operator's go.

partBHeadlineFindings: Row-vs-parcel correction: txgio_parcel carries duplicate rows per (county_fips, prop_id) for ~30% of all rows statewide; a first-pass raw count(*) measurement was caught disagreeing with the already-verified Bastrop parcel count (P-212's 62,257) and discarded before being reported. Final counts use one row per (county_fips, prop_id).

Statewide (deduped, isUsableSitusAddress definition): 83.27% real, 16.18% sentinel, 0.55% none. 'none' is negligible everywhere measured -- the situs gap is a sentinel problem, not an absence problem, confirming the dispatch's framing with a load-bearing breakdown instead of one national number.

Reconciled against the dispatch's own cited 99.3%/89.9% (SS-W5, 2026-08-18): Bastrop is stable across both measurements; Hays/Bell/Bexar/Williamson all show MORE sentinel under this measurement's stricter, product-matching definition (isUsableSitusAddress, which requires a leading house number) than SS-W5's looser one -- expected. Travis is the outlier and the real finding: SS-W5 found only 17.9% real for Travis; this measurement finds 93.6%. Traced to source_vintage: Travis's txgio_parcel rows are stratmap25-landparcels_48453_travis_202508 (an August-2025 edition), while Hays and Bastrop are both on the March-2025 ..._202503 edition; all three counties' CURRENT rows were ingested in the same 2026-09-03 reload (matching the P-212 close's own timestamp for Bastrop). Travis's coverage was already substantially fixed by a full source-vintage upgrade that landed AFTER the SS-W5 sweep, not by an application-side join -- the dispatch's 'named fix was a per-county JOIN' framing is stale for this one county.

The Sturgeon Dr pair itself, live-queried from txgio_parcel: 97651 and 97652 both carry situs_address = 'STURGEON DR, SAN MARCOS, TX 78666' -- present, not absent, missing only the house number; both sit on a real platted geo_id (11-2011-0001-004/00500-3) in the same subdivision as their numbered neighbors 97650/97658. This is the 'street-name-present, house-number-absent' sentinel shape, which is Hays county's DOMINANT sentinel shape (82.6% of Hays sentinels) but is nearly absent in Bastrop (96.4% of Bastrop's sentinels are instead fully blank, ', ,'). The gap is not random: which sentinel SHAPE dominates is itself county-specific.

A third, unrelated data-quality anomaly found and contained (not chased): prop_id='0' is a placeholder/catch-all identity present in 204 of 253 counties (616,287 raw rows statewide, 454,349 of them in Travis alone) whose situs_address sample values are OWNER MAILING addresses, not situs addresses ('TAX DEPT MS 68 198 CHAMPION CT , TX'). The per-parcel dedup this measurement uses collapses every county's prop_id='0' rows to exactly one entry, so it does not distort the reported percentages -- but a naive per-row count (the discarded first pass) would have let it inflate Travis's picture by nearly half a million rows. Named in leave_behind.
